content.use: Add Header and Footer to PDF stamps the same header and footer text on every page of a PDF, which is handy when a document needs a title, a page note or a company name on each page. A teacher adds a class name at the top and a date at the bottom of a handout. An office worker adds a project name at the top and a confidentiality note at the bottom of a report. A shop owner adds a shop name at the top and a phone number at the bottom of a price list. The text is stamped in a small grey font near the top and bottom edges, and the original pages are not changed.
content.tip: Keep the header and footer short, under about 90 characters each, so the text fits on the page. Use the header for a title or project name and the footer for a date or page note. You can fill in only one of the two fields if you need just a header or just a footer.
content.limit: The header and footer are stamped in a fixed small grey font near the top and bottom edges, and you cannot choose the font, size or colour. Very long text is shrunk to fit, and text longer than the page width is cut off. The stamp is added to every page, so you cannot skip a page.
content.example: Adding the header Spring Term 2026 and the footer Page 1 of 10 to a 4-page handout gives a 4-page PDF with the header at the top and the footer at the bottom of every page.
faq: Can I add only a header?
Yes. Fill in the Header text field and leave the Footer text field blank. The tool adds only the header, and the footer is skipped on every page.
Can I add only a footer?
Yes. Fill in the Footer text field and leave the Header text field blank. The tool adds only the footer, and the header is skipped on every page.
Can I change the font or colour?
No. The header and footer use a fixed small grey Helvetica font. You cannot choose the font, size or colour on this page.
Does the stamp cover my page text?
It can, if your page text runs to the very top or bottom edge. The header sits near the top and the footer near the bottom, so pages with wide margins work best.

short.en: Flatten form fields and annotations in a PDF.

tools.meta_description: Flatten a PDF so form fields become permanent text and annotations are removed. Free, private, no uploads.
steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Press Flatten PDF and wait for the status message to say it is done.
Save the downloaded PDF named ak-premium-flattened.pdf.
Open the PDF to check that the form answers are now part of the page, because flattening cannot be undone.

content.use: Flatten PDF turns form fields and annotations in a PDF into permanent page content, so the filled-in answers and notes can no longer be changed or removed. A student flattens a filled application form before sending it, so the answers cannot be edited by mistake. An office worker flattens a signed form so the signature stays as it is. A shop owner flattens a price list with notes so the notes print exactly as shown. Form fields become plain text on the page, and annotations such as comments and links are removed. The flattened PDF looks the same, but nothing in it can be edited as a form any more.
content.tip: Keep a copy of the original PDF before you flatten it, because flattening cannot be undone. Flatten a form only after every field is filled in, because empty fields become blank text. Check the flattened PDF before you send it, to make sure every answer is still readable.
content.limit: Flattening cannot be undone, so keep a copy of the original. Form fields become plain text and can no longer be edited or filled in. Annotations such as comments, highlights and links are removed. A password-protected PDF must be unlocked first.
content.example: Flattening a 2-page application form with 10 filled fields gives a 2-page PDF where the answers are now part of the page and cannot be changed.
faq: What does flattening a PDF do?
It turns form fields into permanent text on the page and removes annotations. The PDF looks the same, but the fields can no longer be edited or filled in.
Can I undo flattening?
No. Flattening is permanent. Keep a copy of the original PDF before you flatten it, because the form fields cannot be restored afterwards.
Does flattening change how the PDF looks?
No. The filled-in answers stay where they were, as plain text on the page. Only the ability to edit them is gone, and annotations such as comments are removed.
Can I flatten a protected PDF?
No. A password-protected PDF must be unlocked first. Use Unlock PDF with the password, then flatten the unlocked file. The unlocked file is a normal PDF that this tool can open.

short.en: View and edit a PDF's title, author and more.

tools.meta_description: View and edit a PDF's title, author, subject and keywords, in your browser. Free, private, no uploads.
steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Read the current title, author, subject and keywords shown under Current metadata, and check the fields are filled in with them.
Change the Title, Author, Subject or Keywords fields to the values you want.
Press Update Metadata.
Save the downloaded PDF, which has the new metadata and the same pages.

content.use: PDF Metadata Editor shows and changes the hidden details of a PDF, such as its title, author, subject and keywords. A student sets the title and author of an assignment PDF so it shows the right name in a reader. An office worker sets the subject of a report PDF so it is easy to find later. A shop owner sets keywords on a price list PDF so it turns up in a search. The metadata is the text a PDF reader shows in the document properties, and it does not change the pages themselves. The edited PDF is saved with the same pages and layout, only the details are new.
content.tip: Fill in the title and author first, because those are the details most readers show. Use keywords that describe the document, separated by commas, so it is easy to find later. Leave a field blank if you want that detail removed from the PDF.
content.limit: Only the title, author, subject and keywords can be changed. The producer, creator and dates are not edited by this tool. A password-protected PDF must be unlocked first. Some PDF readers may still show old details if they cached the file.
content.example: Setting the title to Spring Term Report, the author to Ayesha Khan and the keywords to term report, spring 2026 on a 6-page PDF gives a 6-page PDF with those details in its properties.
faq: What is PDF metadata?
It is the hidden detail stored in a PDF, such as its title, author, subject and keywords. A PDF reader shows it in the document properties, and search tools can use it to find the file.
Does editing metadata change my pages?
No. The pages, text and layout stay exactly the same. Only the title, author, subject and keywords stored in the file are changed.
Can I remove a detail?
Yes. Leave that field blank and press Update Metadata. The blank detail is removed from the PDF, and the other details are kept.
Can I edit a protected PDF?
No. A password-protected PDF must be unlocked first. Use Unlock PDF with the password, then edit the metadata of the unlocked file.

short.en: Scale every page to A4, Letter or Legal.

tools.meta_description: Scale every page of a PDF to A4, Letter or Legal, in your browser. Free, private, no uploads.
steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Pick a page size from the Page size list: A4, Letter or Legal.
Press Resize Pages.
Save the downloaded PDF, which has every page at the size you picked.

content.use: Resize PDF Page Size scales every page of a PDF to A4, Letter or Legal, which is handy when a PDF was made for a different paper size and needs to print cleanly. A student resizes a US Letter assignment to A4 so it prints correctly on local paper. An office worker resizes an A4 report to Letter for a client in the United States. A shop owner resizes a Legal-size price list to A4 for a local printer. Each page is scaled to fit the new size, keeping its shape, and centred on the page. The text and pictures are scaled with the page, so nothing is cropped.
content.tip: Pick the size your printer uses before you resize, because A4 is the usual size in Pakistan and Letter is the usual size in the United States. If the original page is a very different shape, the scaled page has small margins on two sides. Check the resized PDF before you print it.
content.limit: Each page is scaled to fit the new size, keeping its shape, so a page of a very different shape has small margins on two sides. Form fields and links are not carried over to the resized pages. A password-protected PDF must be unlocked first.
content.example: Resizing a 3-page US Letter assignment to A4 gives a 3-page PDF at A4 size (595 by 842 points), with each page scaled to fit and centred.
faq: What sizes can I choose?
A4, Letter and Legal. A4 is 595 by 842 points, Letter is 612 by 792 points, and Legal is 612 by 1008 points. Pick the size your printer uses.
Does resizing crop my pages?
No. Each page is scaled to fit the new size, keeping its shape, and centred on the page. Nothing is cropped, but a page of a very different shape has small margins on two sides.
Does resizing change my text?
No. The text and pictures are scaled with the page, so they stay in the same place relative to each other. Only the page size and the scale change.
Can I resize a protected PDF?
No. A password-protected PDF must be unlocked first. Use Unlock PDF with the password, then resize the unlocked file. The unlocked file is a normal PDF that this tool can open.

tools.meta_description: Turn PNG images into JPG in your browser, free and private. Transparent parts become white.
steps: Choose a PNG image with the file button.
Check the file name shown under the button is the right image.
Press Convert PNG to JPG.
Save the downloaded JPG, which has the same width and height as the PNG.

content.use: PNG to JPG turns a PNG picture into a JPG file, keeping the same width and height. A student turns a PNG screenshot into a JPG to upload to a portal that only takes JPG files. A shop owner turns product PNGs into JPGs so the online shop loads faster. An office worker turns a PNG chart into a JPG to paste into a report. JPG files are much smaller than PNG files, so they are easier to send and upload. The picture is converted in your browser with the canvas, so your image is never uploaded anywhere and you do not need an account.
content.tip: Use PNG to JPG when you need a smaller file for upload or sharing. If your PNG has transparency, remember the see-through parts become white in JPG, so convert to PNG instead if you need to keep transparency. For the sharpest result, start from a clear PNG; a blurry picture stays blurry after conversion.
content.limit: Only PNG images are accepted, and each file must be under 50 MB. JPG has no transparency, so see-through parts of the PNG become white. The picture keeps its original width and height; this tool does not resize it.
content.example: Converting a 1200 by 800 PNG screenshot gives a 1200 by 800 JPG file that is much smaller and ready to upload.
faq: What happens to transparency in JPG?
It becomes white. JPG has no transparency, so the see-through parts of your PNG become white. Convert to PNG or WebP instead if you need to keep the transparency.
Does the JPG keep the same size?
Yes. The width and height stay exactly the same as the PNG. Only the file format changes. Use Image Resizer if you also need a different size.
Can I convert several PNG images at once?
No. This page converts one PNG image at a time. Choose one image, press Convert PNG to JPG, save the result, then choose the next image.
What name does the JPG download with?
ak-premium-png-to-jpg.jpg. It has the same width and height as your PNG, and your original PNG file is not changed in any way.

tools.meta_description: Turn JPG images into PNG in your browser, free and private. The picture keeps its size.
steps: Choose a JPG image with the file button.
Check the file name shown under the button is the right image.
Press Convert JPG to PNG.
Save the downloaded PNG, which has the same width and height as the JPG.

content.use: JPG to PNG turns a JPG photo into a PNG file, keeping the same width and height. A designer turns a JPG photo into PNG to edit it in a program that needs PNG. A student turns a JPG screenshot into PNG so text in the picture stays sharp. An office worker turns a JPG chart into PNG to print it without JPG smudges. PNG is lossless, so the picture keeps all its detail, though the file is usually larger than the JPG. The conversion runs in your browser with the canvas, so your photo is never uploaded anywhere and you do not need an account.
content.tip: Use JPG to PNG when you need a lossless copy or sharp text. The PNG file is usually larger than the JPG, so keep the JPG if you only need to share the photo. A JPG photo that is already blurry will not become sharp as a PNG.
content.limit: Only JPG and JPEG images are accepted, and each file must be under 50 MB. PNG is lossless, so the file is usually larger than the JPG. The picture keeps its original width and height; this tool does not resize it.
content.example: Converting a 1200 by 800 JPG photo gives a 1200 by 800 PNG file with the same picture and no JPG smudges.
faq: Will the PNG be better quality than the JPG?
No. PNG is lossless, but it cannot add detail that the JPG already lost. The PNG keeps exactly the detail in your JPG, without adding new JPG smudges.
Why is the PNG file larger?
PNG is lossless, so it stores every pixel exactly. JPG throws away detail to make a smaller file. The PNG keeps all the detail, so it is usually larger than the same picture as a JPG.
Can I convert several JPG images at once?
No. This page converts one JPG image at a time. Choose one image, press Convert JPG to PNG, save the result, then choose the next image.
What name does the PNG download with?
ak-premium-jpg-to-png.png. It has the same width and height as your JPG, and your original JPG file is not changed in any way.

tools.meta_description: Turn WebP images into JPG in your browser, free and private. Works for photos saved as WebP.
steps: Choose a WebP image with the file button.
Check the file name shown under the button is the right image.
Press Convert WebP to JPG.
Save the downloaded JPG, which has the same width and height as the WebP.

content.use: WebP to JPG turns a WebP picture into a JPG file, keeping the same width and height. Many websites and phones save photos as WebP, but some portals, printers and old programs only accept JPG. A student turns a WebP screenshot into a JPG to upload to a portal that only takes JPG. A shop owner turns WebP product photos into JPGs for a marketplace that does not take WebP. The conversion runs in your browser with the canvas, so your image is never uploaded anywhere and you do not need an account.
content.tip: Use WebP to JPG when a site or program refuses WebP files. If your WebP has transparency, the see-through parts become white in JPG, so convert to PNG instead to keep transparency. WebP files are usually small, so the JPG may be larger than the WebP.
content.limit: Only WebP images are accepted, and each file must be under 50 MB. JPG has no transparency, so see-through parts of the WebP become white. The picture keeps its original width and height; this tool does not resize it.
content.example: Converting a 1200 by 800 WebP screenshot gives a 1200 by 800 JPG file that uploads to a portal that only accepts JPG.
faq: Why do some sites not accept WebP?
WebP is newer than JPG, so some portals, printers and old programs only accept JPG or PNG. Converting to JPG gives you a file those sites accept, with the same picture.
Does the JPG lose quality?
A little. JPG throws away some detail to make a smaller file, while WebP keeps more. The picture looks the same at normal size, but fine detail can soften slightly.
Can I convert several WebP images at once?
No. This page converts one WebP image at a time. Choose one image, press Convert WebP to JPG, save the result, then choose the next image.
Where does the JPG download go?
To your browser download folder, as ak-premium-webp-to-jpg.jpg. It has the same width and height as your WebP, and your original WebP file is not changed.

tools.meta_description: Turn WebP images into PNG in your browser, free and private. Transparency is kept.
steps: Choose a WebP image with the file button.
Check the file name shown under the button is the right image.
Press Convert WebP to PNG.
Save the downloaded PNG, which has the same width and height as the WebP.

content.use: WebP to PNG turns a WebP picture into a PNG file, keeping the same width and height and keeping transparency. A designer turns a WebP logo into PNG to edit it in a program that needs PNG. A student turns a WebP screenshot into PNG so text stays sharp. An office worker turns a WebP chart into PNG to print it without smudges. PNG is lossless, so the picture keeps all its detail, though the file is usually larger than the WebP. The conversion runs in your browser with the canvas, so your image is never uploaded anywhere and you do not need an account.
content.tip: Use WebP to PNG when you need transparency or a lossless copy. The PNG is usually larger than the WebP, so keep the WebP if you only need to share the picture. A WebP that is already blurry will not become sharp as a PNG.
content.limit: Only WebP images are accepted, and each file must be under 50 MB. PNG is lossless, so the file is usually larger than the WebP. The picture keeps its original width and height; this tool does not resize it.
content.example: Converting a 1200 by 800 WebP screenshot gives a 1200 by 800 PNG file with sharp text and no smudges.
faq: Does the PNG keep the see-through parts?
Yes. WebP to PNG keeps the see-through parts of your WebP picture. That is the main reason to choose PNG instead of JPG, because JPG has no transparency and turns see-through parts white.
Why is the PNG file larger than the WebP?
PNG is lossless, so it stores every pixel exactly. WebP throws away some detail to make a smaller file. The PNG keeps all the detail, so it is usually larger than the same picture as a WebP.
Which format should I pick, PNG or JPG?
Pick PNG if you need transparency or sharp text, and JPG if you need the smallest file for upload. WebP to PNG keeps transparency; WebP to JPG gives a smaller file but turns see-through parts white.
Where is the downloaded PNG saved?
In your browser download folder, as ak-premium-webp-to-png.png. It has the same width and height as your WebP, and your original WebP file is not changed.

tools.meta_description: Turn JPG images into WebP in your browser, free and private. Smaller files for the web.
steps: Choose a JPG image with the file button.
Check the file name shown under the button is the right image.
Press Convert JPG to WebP.
Save the downloaded WebP, which has the same width and height as the JPG.

content.use: JPG to WebP turns a JPG photo into a WebP file, keeping the same width and height. WebP files are much smaller than JPG files, so they load faster on a website. A shop owner turns product JPGs into WebP so the online shop loads faster. A blogger turns JPG photos into WebP so readers on slow connections still see the pictures quickly. A student turns JPG screenshots into WebP to send them in a chat without using much data. The conversion runs in your browser with the canvas, so your photo is never uploaded anywhere and you do not need an account.
content.tip: Use JPG to WebP when you need smaller files for a website or a chat. WebP is supported by all modern browsers, but some old programs do not open it, so keep the JPG too if you are not sure. A JPG that is already blurry will not become sharp as a WebP.
content.limit: Only JPG and JPEG images are accepted, and each file must be under 50 MB. The picture keeps its original width and height; this tool does not resize it. Some old programs cannot open WebP, so keep your JPG if you need to use the picture there.
content.example: Converting a 1200 by 800 JPG photo gives a 1200 by 800 WebP file that is much smaller and loads faster on a website.
faq: How much smaller is the WebP file?

Usually much smaller than the JPG, often by a third or more, because WebP compresses photos better. The exact saving depends on the picture; a photo with lots of detail saves less than a plain screenshot.
Can old programs open WebP?
Most modern browsers open WebP, but some old photo programs and printers do not. If you are not sure, keep the JPG as well, or convert back with WebP to JPG.
Does WebP lose quality?
A little. WebP at this quality setting keeps the picture looking the same at normal size, but fine detail can soften slightly, just like JPG. The width and height do not change.
What name does the WebP download with?
ak-premium-jpg-to-webp.webp. It has the same width and height as your JPG, and your original JPG file is not changed in any way.

short.en: Turn SVG files into PNG images.

tools.meta_description: Turn SVG files into PNG images in your browser, free and private. Choose the output width.
steps: Choose an SVG file with the file button.
Enter the output width in pixels in the Width box, or leave 1024.
Press Convert SVG to PNG.
Save the downloaded PNG, which has the width you entered and the same shape as the SVG.

content.use: SVG to PNG turns a vector SVG file into a PNG picture at the width you choose. A designer turns a logo SVG into a PNG to use it in a document or a presentation that does not take SVG. A shop owner turns an SVG icon into a PNG to put it on a website. A student turns an SVG diagram into a PNG to paste it into an assignment. The PNG keeps the shape of the SVG, and a bigger width gives a sharper picture. The conversion runs in your browser, so your file is never uploaded anywhere and you do not need an account.
content.tip: Use a bigger width for a sharper PNG, because the SVG is drawn fresh at that size. Leave the width at 1024 for most uses. If the PNG comes out blank, your SVG may use an external image or font that the browser cannot load here.
content.limit: Only SVG files are accepted, and each file must be under 50 MB. The PNG keeps the SVG shape, but text in the SVG uses your browser fonts, so it can look different from the original program. SVGs that link to external images or fonts cannot be drawn and give an error.
content.example: Converting a logo SVG at width 1024 gives a PNG that is 1024 pixels wide, with the same shape as the logo, ready to paste into a document.
faq: Why is my PNG blank or missing parts?
Your SVG probably links to an external image or font that the browser cannot load here. Save the SVG with its images and fonts embedded, or use a plain SVG with shapes and text only.
What width should I enter?
1024 pixels works for most uses. Enter a bigger width, such as 2048, for a sharper picture or a large print. The height follows the SVG shape automatically.
Does the PNG keep transparency?
Yes. If your SVG has see-through parts, the PNG keeps them see-through. The PNG is saved with transparency, so you can place it on any background.
Can I convert an SVG with text in it?
Yes, but the text is drawn with your browser fonts, so it can look different from the original program. For an exact match, turn the text into shapes in your drawing program first.

short.en: Crop an image to the part you need.

tools.meta_description: Crop an image in your browser, free and private. Drag to choose the area, then download a PNG.
steps: Choose a JPG, PNG or WebP image with the file button.
Drag on the preview to draw the rectangle you want to keep.
Fine-tune the rectangle with the X, Y, Width and Height boxes.
Press Crop Image.
Save the downloaded PNG, which holds only the rectangle you chose.

content.use: Image Cropper cuts a picture down to the part you want, and saves it as a PNG. A student crops a screenshot to keep only one diagram for an assignment. A shop owner crops a product photo to remove the messy background around it. A job applicant crops a photo to keep only their face for a profile picture. You drag a rectangle on the preview, and the numbers in the X, Y, Width and Height boxes show exactly which part is kept. The crop runs in your browser with the canvas, so your photo is never uploaded anywhere and you do not need an account.
content.tip: Drag on the preview to draw the rectangle, then use the X, Y, Width and Height boxes to set it exactly. Keep the rectangle inside the picture; numbers that go past the edge are pulled back inside. The output is always PNG, which keeps the picture sharp.
content.limit: JPG, PNG and WebP images are accepted, and each file must be under 50 MB. The output is always a PNG file, even if you cropped a JPG. The crop keeps only the rectangle you drew; the rest of the picture is thrown away, so keep a copy of the original.
content.example: Cropping a 1200 by 800 screenshot to a 600 by 400 rectangle gives a 600 by 400 PNG with only the diagram you selected.
faq: How do I choose the crop area?
Drag on the preview with your mouse or finger to draw a rectangle. The X, Y, Width and Height boxes show the rectangle in pixels, and you can type new numbers there to set it exactly.
Why is the output a PNG file?
PNG is lossless, so the cropped picture keeps all its detail. Even if you cropped a JPG, the result is a PNG. Use Image Converter afterwards if you need a JPG.
Can I crop to an exact size?
Yes. Type the exact Width and Height in pixels in the boxes, and set X and Y to place the rectangle. Press Crop Image and the PNG will have exactly that width and height.
Can I undo a crop?
No. The crop throws away everything outside the rectangle. Keep a copy of the original picture, or choose the same image again and draw a new rectangle.

short.en: Rotate or flip an image in your browser.

tools.meta_description: Rotate or flip an image in your browser, free and private. Turn it left or right, or mirror it.
steps: Choose a JPG, PNG or WebP image with the file button.
Press Rotate Left or Rotate Right to turn the picture, or Flip Horizontal or Flip Vertical to mirror it.
Pick the output format, PNG or JPEG, in the Output format box.
Press Download Image.
Save the downloaded picture, which has the rotation and flip you applied.

content.use: Rotate and Flip Image turns a picture left or right, or mirrors it, without changing anything else. A student rotates a sideways photo of handwritten notes so it reads the right way up. A shop owner flips a product photo to match the layout of a web page. A job applicant rotates a scanned certificate that came out sideways. Each press of Rotate Left or Rotate Right turns the picture by 90 degrees, and Flip Horizontal or Flip Vertical mirrors it. The changes run in your browser with the canvas, so your photo is never uploaded anywhere and you do not need an account.
content.tip: Press Rotate Right once for a photo that is sideways clockwise, or three times for one that is sideways the other way. Flip Horizontal mirrors a picture left to right, which is useful for a selfie that looks reversed. Choose JPEG for photos and PNG if you need transparency.
content.limit: JPG, PNG and WebP images are accepted, and each file must be under 50 MB. Rotating by 90 degrees swaps the width and height. Saving as JPEG flattens transparency onto a white background, because JPG has no transparency.
content.example: Rotating a 800 by 1200 sideways photo once to the right gives a 1200 by 800 photo that reads the right way up.
faq: How many times do I press Rotate Right?
Once for a photo that is sideways clockwise, twice to turn it upside down, and three times for a photo that is sideways the other way. Each press turns the picture by 90 degrees.
What is the difference between flip and rotate?
Rotate turns the picture around, so the top becomes a side. Flip mirrors it, so the left and right swap but the top stays on top. A flipped photo is a mirror image, not a rotated one.
Why is the width and height swapped?

Rotating by 90 degrees turns the picture on its side, so the old width becomes the new height and the old height becomes the new width. Rotating twice, by 180 degrees, keeps the width and height the same.
Which output format should I pick?
Pick JPEG for photos, because it makes smaller files. Pick PNG if your picture has transparency or sharp text, because PNG keeps both exactly. JPEG turns see-through parts white.

short.en: Make a passport photo at the right size.

tools.meta_description: Make a passport photo at the right size for Pakistan, India, USA, UK, EU, UAE or Canada, in your browser.
steps: Choose a clear front-facing photo with the file button.
Pick your country in the Country box, such as Pakistan, USA or Canada.
Check the size shown under the Country box matches your form.
Press Make Passport Photo.
Save the downloaded JPG, which has the exact size for that country.

content.use: Passport Photo Maker cuts your photo to the exact passport size for your country and saves it as a JPG. Pakistan, UK, EU and UAE use 35 by 45 mm, which is 413 by 531 pixels. India and the USA use 2 by 2 inches, which is 600 by 600 pixels. Canada uses 50 by 70 mm, which is 591 by 827 pixels. The tool crops the centre of your photo to the right shape and resizes it to the exact pixels, so you can print it or upload it to a form. The photo is made in your browser, so your picture is never uploaded anywhere and you do not need an account.
content.tip: Use a clear photo taken against a plain light background, with your face in the centre and looking at the camera. The tool crops the centre, so keep your face in the middle of the photo. Check the size on your official form before you print or submit, because rules change.
content.limit: JPG, PNG and WebP photos are accepted, and each file must be under 50 MB. The tool only sets the size and shape; it cannot fix a blurry photo, bad light or a wrong background, and it cannot guarantee a form will accept the photo. Sizes follow the common official rules, but always check your form, because some visas use a different size.
content.example: Choosing a photo and picking Pakistan gives a 413 by 531 pixel JPG, which is 35 by 45 mm, ready to print or upload.
faq: What size is a Pakistan passport photo?
35 by 45 mm, which is 413 by 531 pixels. Pick Pakistan in the Country box and the tool makes a JPG at exactly that size.
What size is a USA passport photo?
2 by 2 inches, which is 51 by 51 mm or 600 by 600 pixels. Pick USA in the Country box and the tool makes a square JPG at exactly that size.
Why is my face cut off?
The tool crops the centre of your photo to the passport shape. Use a photo with your face in the centre and some space around it, so the crop keeps your whole face.
Will my form accept this photo?
The tool sets the exact size for the country you pick, but acceptance also depends on light, background, expression and the form rules. Check the official photo rules on your form before you submit.

short.en: Convert length, weight, temperature and more.

tools.meta_description: Convert length, weight, temperature, area, volume, speed, data, time and energy in your browser.
steps: Choose the kind of unit in the 'Unit type' list, such as Length or Weight.
Type the number in the 'Value' box.
Choose the unit you have in the 'From' list and the unit you want in the 'To' list.
Press Convert Units, or just wait, because the result updates as you type.
Read the answer under the button, shown with both units.

content.use: Unit Converter changes a measurement from one unit to another in your browser. A student changes 5 kilometres into metres for a homework answer. A cook changes 250 grams into ounces for a recipe from another country. A traveller changes miles into kilometres to read a road sign. A shop owner changes square feet into square metres for a floor plan. You pick the kind of unit, type the number, choose the unit you have and the unit you want, and the answer appears at once. Length, weight, temperature, area, volume, speed, data, time and energy are all covered, so most everyday conversions are one page away.
content.tip: For recipes, check whether the book uses US cups or metric cups before you convert volume. For temperature, remember that 0 degrees Celsius is 32 degrees Fahrenheit, so the two scales do not start at the same place. Data units here use 1024, so 1 MB is 1024 KB, which is how computers count storage.
content.limit: Only one number is converted at a time, and the result is rounded to 4 decimal places. Temperature uses Celsius, Fahrenheit and Kelvin only. Data units use 1024 per step, not 1000, and volume uses US cups and gallons.
content.example: Choosing Length, typing 5, and converting kilometres to metres gives 5 km = 5000 m.
faq: How do I convert kilometres to miles?
Choose Length, type the kilometres, set From to kilometres and To to miles, then press Convert Units. The answer shows the miles at once.
Why is 0 Celsius not 0 Fahrenheit?
The two scales start at different places. Water freezes at 0 degrees Celsius and 32 degrees Fahrenheit, so 0 Celsius is 32 Fahrenheit, not zero.
Does it convert kilograms to pounds?
Yes. Choose Weight, type the kilograms, set From to kilograms and To to pounds. One kilogram is about 2.20 pounds.
Can I convert square feet to square metres?
Yes. Choose Area, type the square feet, set From to square feet and To to square metres. The answer is rounded to 4 decimal places.

short.en: Work out sale prices and savings.

tools.meta_description: Work out the discount amount and the final sale price from any price and percent.
steps: Type the original price in the 'Original price' box.
Type the discount percent in the 'Discount (%)' box.
Press Calculate Discount, or just wait, because the result updates as you type.
Read the discount amount and the final price under the button.

content.use: Discount Calculator works out how much you save in a sale and what you actually pay. A shopper sees a shirt marked 20 percent off and wants the real price before buying. A shop owner sets a sale price that still leaves a profit. A student checks whether a 50 percent off deal is really half price. You type the original price and the discount percent, and the tool shows the discount amount and the price you pay. It works for any currency, because it only uses the numbers you type.
content.tip: A 20 percent discount means you pay 80 percent of the price, so you can check the answer by working out 80 percent of the price. For two discounts in a row, apply the first discount, then apply the second discount to the new price, not to the original price. Round the final price to your local currency before you pay.
content.limit: The discount percent must be between 0 and 100. The tool does not add tax or delivery charges, so the price it shows is before tax. It only uses the numbers you type, so check that the original price is right.
content.example: A price of 1000 with a 20 percent discount gives a discount of 200 and a final price of 800.
faq: How do I find the price after discount?
Type the original price and the discount percent, then press Calculate Discount. The final price is shown next to the discount amount.
What is 25 percent off 400?
The discount is 100 and the final price is 300. Type 400 as the price and 25 as the discount percent to see it.
Can the discount be more than 100 percent?
No. A discount above 100 percent would make the price negative, so the tool only accepts 0 to 100 percent.
Does it add tax to the price?
No. The tool shows the price before tax. Add your local tax to the final price yourself if you need the total you will pay.

short.en: See how savings grow over time.

tools.meta_description: See how savings grow with compound interest over years, with any compounding frequency.
steps: Type the starting amount in the 'Principal amount' box.
Type the yearly interest rate in the 'Annual interest rate (%)' box.
Type the number of years and choose how often interest is added in the 'Compounding' list.
Press Calculate Compound Interest, or just wait, because the result updates as you type.
Read the maturity amount and the interest earned under the button.

content.use: Compound Interest Calculator shows how savings grow when the interest itself earns interest. A saver puts money in a bank account and wants to know what it becomes in 5 years. A parent plans a fund for a child and compares yearly and monthly compounding. A student learns why starting early matters more than saving more later. You type the starting amount, the yearly rate, the years, and how often interest is added, and the tool shows the final amount and the interest earned.
content.tip: Monthly compounding grows slightly faster than yearly compounding at the same rate, because interest starts earning interest sooner. The rate you type should be the yearly rate the bank quotes. This tool assumes you add no more money and take nothing out during the years.
content.limit: The tool assumes a fixed rate and no deposits or withdrawals after the start. Real bank rates change, and tax or fees are not included, so the result is an estimate. The rate must be 0 or more and the years must be more than 0.
content.example: 100,000 at 10 percent a year for 5 years, compounded yearly, grows to 161,051, with 61,051 interest earned.
faq: What is compound interest?
It is interest earned on both the starting amount and the interest already added. Each time interest is added, the next interest is worked out on the bigger amount.
Is monthly compounding better than yearly?
Yes, slightly. With monthly compounding the interest starts earning interest sooner, so the same rate gives a slightly bigger final amount.
Does it include tax on the interest?
No. The tool shows the amount before tax. Your bank or tax office may take tax from the interest, so the money you keep can be less.
Can I add monthly deposits with this tool?
No. This tool works out growth on one starting amount only. It does not add regular deposits or withdrawals, so use a savings plan calculator if you add money every month.

short.en: Work out your monthly home loan payment.

tools.meta_description: Work out the monthly payment, total paid and total interest on a home loan.
steps: Type the loan amount in the 'Loan amount' box.
Type the yearly interest rate in the 'Annual interest rate (%)' box.
Type the loan length in years in the 'Loan term (years)' box.
Press Calculate Monthly Payment, or just wait, because the result updates as you type.
Read the monthly payment, the total paid and the total interest under the button.

content.use: Mortgage Calculator works out the monthly payment on a home loan. A buyer checks whether the monthly payment fits the family budget before choosing a house. A family compares a 20 year loan with a 30 year loan to see the difference in payment and total interest. An owner checks how much of each payment goes to interest in the early years. You type the loan amount, the yearly interest rate and the years, and the tool shows the monthly payment, the total paid and the total interest.
content.tip: A longer loan means a smaller monthly payment but much more total interest, so compare both numbers before you choose. A small rise in the rate can add a lot to the monthly payment on a big loan. The payment here is principal plus interest only; taxes and insurance are not included.
content.limit: The payment shown is principal and interest only. It does not include property tax, insurance or other charges your lender may add. The rate is assumed fixed for the whole loan, so a variable rate loan will differ.
content.example: A loan of 5,000,000 at 12 percent a year for 20 years gives a monthly payment of 55,054.31.
faq: How is the monthly payment worked out?
It uses the standard loan formula with the yearly rate divided by 12 and the number of monthly payments. The payment stays the same every month for a fixed rate loan.
Why is the total interest so high?
Interest is charged on the amount you still owe, which is large in the early years. Over 20 years the interest adds up to a large share of the total paid.
Does it include property tax?
No. The payment shown is principal and interest only. Add your property tax and insurance yourself to get the full monthly cost.
What happens if the rate changes?
This tool assumes a fixed rate. If your loan has a variable rate, the monthly payment will change when the rate changes, so work it out again with the new rate.

short.en: Split the bill and work out the tip.

tools.meta_description: Work out the tip, the total bill and the amount each person pays when you split it.
steps: Type the bill amount in the 'Bill amount' box.
Type the tip percent in the 'Tip (%)' box.
Type the number of people in the 'Split between (people)' box.
Press Calculate Tip, or just wait, because the result updates as you type.
Read the tip, the total and the amount per person under the button.

content.use: Tip Calculator works out the tip on a restaurant bill and splits the total fairly. Friends share a dinner bill and want to know what each person pays with the tip included. A traveller in another country wants to leave the right tip without doing the maths by hand. A family checks the total before paying by card. You type the bill, the tip percent and the number of people, and the tool shows the tip, the total and the amount per person.
content.tip: A 10 percent tip is easy to check: move the decimal point one place left on the bill. If the service was poor, you can set the tip to 0 and just split the bill. In some countries a service charge is already added to the bill, so check before you tip on top of it.
content.limit: The tip percent must be 0 or more and the number of people must be at least 1. The tool does not add tax, so use the bill amount before or after tax as you prefer. Amounts are rounded to 2 decimal places, so a few cents may differ when you split.
content.example: A bill of 2000 with a 15 percent tip and 4 people gives a tip of 300, a total of 2300, and 575 per person.
faq: How much should I tip at a restaurant?
It depends on the country. In many places 10 to 15 percent is common, and 15 to 20 percent is common in the United States. Check local custom before you tip.
How do I split a bill between friends?
Type the bill, the tip percent and the number of people. The tool shows the amount each person pays, including the tip.
Does the tip include tax?
No. The tool works out the tip on the bill amount you type. If you want the tip on the amount before tax, type the bill before tax.
Can I tip 0 percent?
Yes. Set the tip to 0 and the tool splits just the bill. The tip amount shows as 0 and the total is the same as the bill.

short.en: Convert times between world time zones.

tools.meta_description: Convert a date and time between world time zones, with daylight saving handled.
steps: Pick the date in the 'Date' box and the time in the 'Time' box.
Choose the zone the time is in, in the 'From time zone' list.
Choose the zone you want in the 'To time zone' list.
Press Convert Time Zone, or just wait, because the result updates as you type.
Read the converted date and time under the button.

content.use: Time Zone Converter changes a time from one part of the world to another. A worker in Lahore joins a call with a team in London and needs the right time. A student applies to a university abroad and must not miss a deadline in another time zone. A family calls relatives overseas and wants to avoid waking them up. You pick the date and time, choose the zone you have and the zone you want, and the tool shows the converted time, with daylight saving handled for you.
content.tip: Daylight saving changes the gap between zones in summer and winter, so always include the date, not just the time. London is 5 hours behind Lahore in winter but 4 hours behind in summer. If the converted time falls on another day, the tool shows the new date too.
content.limit: The tool uses the time zone rules built into your browser, which are kept up to date by your system. Very old or future dates may use rules that have changed. It converts clock times only; it does not book meetings or send invites.
content.example: 12:00 on 15 January 2026 in Lahore is 07:00 on 15 January 2026 in London.
faq: What is the time difference between Lahore and London?
It is 5 hours in winter and 4 hours in summer, because London uses daylight saving and Lahore does not. Pick a date to get the right gap.
Does it handle daylight saving time?
Yes. The tool uses your browser's time zone rules, so daylight saving is applied for the date you pick, and the gap between two zones can change with the season.
Can I convert to New York time?
Yes. Choose America/New_York in the To list. New York is 10 hours behind Lahore in winter and 9 hours behind in summer.
Why does the date change sometimes?
When the converted time crosses midnight, the date moves to the next day or the day before. The tool always shows the full date with the time.

short.en: Count days, weeks and months between dates.

tools.meta_description: Count the days, weeks and months between any two dates in your browser.
steps: Pick the first date in the 'From date' box.
Pick the second date in the 'To date' box.
Press Calculate Difference, or just wait, because the result updates as you type.
Read the days, weeks and months under the button.

content.use: Date Difference Calculator counts the time between two dates. A worker counts the days left before a project deadline. A parent counts the days until a child's birthday. A student counts the weeks between the start and the end of a term. A traveller counts the days of a trip. You pick the two dates and the tool shows the days between them, the weeks and days, and the full months, so you can plan without counting on a calendar.
content.tip: The count is the number of days from the first date to the second date, not including the first date. If you need to include both end days, add 1 to the day count. The order of the two dates does not matter; the tool always counts the gap between them.
content.limit: The tool counts whole days between the dates you pick. It does not count working days or skip weekends and holidays. Very old dates may use calendar rules that differ from today's calendar.
content.example: From 1 January 2025 to 1 January 2026 is 365 days, which is 52 weeks and 1 day.
faq: How many days are between two dates?
Pick the two dates and press Calculate Difference. The tool shows the exact number of days, plus the weeks and days and the full months.
Does it count the first date?
No. The count is the days from the first date to the second date. If you want to include both end days, add 1 to the day count.
Can I count weeks instead of days?
Yes. The result shows the weeks and the extra days as well, so 365 days shows as 52 weeks and 1 day.
Does the order of the dates matter?
No. The tool always counts the gap between the two dates, whichever one you pick first, so you can enter them in any order you like.

short.en: Work out your daily calorie needs.

tools.meta_description: Estimate your BMR and daily calorie needs (TDEE) from age, height, weight and activity.
steps: Type your age in the 'Age (years)' box.
Choose your sex in the 'Sex' list and type your height and weight.
Choose your activity level in the 'Activity level' list.
Press Calculate Calories, or just wait, because the result updates as you type.
Read your BMR and TDEE in calories a day under the button.

content.use: Calorie and TDEE Calculator estimates how many calories your body uses in a day. A person starting a diet wants a daily target that fits their body and activity. A gym member checks whether they eat enough to build muscle. A student learns the difference between BMR, the calories the body uses at rest, and TDEE, the total with daily activity. You type your age, sex, height and weight, choose your activity level, and the tool shows your BMR and TDEE.
content.tip: TDEE is the number to use for a daily calorie target, not BMR, because BMR leaves out all movement. Choose the activity level that matches a normal week, not your busiest day. A small change in weight or activity changes the result, so update the numbers as they change.
content.limit: These numbers are estimates from the Mifflin-St Jeor formula, not medical advice. They do not fit everyone, including children, pregnant people, and people with some health conditions. For a personal diet or health plan, talk to a doctor or a qualified dietitian.
content.example: A 30-year-old man, 180 cm tall and 80 kg, moderately active, has a BMR of 1780 calories a day and a TDEE of 2759 calories a day.
faq: What is the difference between BMR and TDEE?
BMR is the calories your body uses at rest to stay alive. TDEE adds your daily activity and movement, so it is the total calories you use in a day.
How many calories do I need to lose weight?
Most people aim for a TDEE minus about 300 to 500 calories a day. This tool only gives the estimate; a doctor or dietitian can set a safe target for you.
Which activity level should I choose?
Pick the level that matches a normal week. Desk work with little exercise is sedentary, while a physical job or daily training is very active.
Is this medical advice?
No. The numbers are estimates from a standard formula. They are not a diagnosis or a diet plan, so talk to a doctor for personal advice.

short.en: Sin, cos, log, powers and more.

tools.meta_description: A free scientific calculator with sin, cos, tan, log, square root and powers.
steps: Tap the number and operator keys to build your sum in the display.
Tap a function key such as sin, cos, log or sqrt to add it to the sum.
Tap the pi or e key when you need those numbers.
Press = to work out the answer, or C to clear the display.
Read the result under the display.

content.use: Scientific Calculator does the maths a basic calculator cannot. A student works out sin of 30 degrees for a trigonometry problem. An engineer takes the log of a number for a decibel calculation. A shop owner works out a power for a compound growth check. You tap the keys to build the sum, use the function keys for sin, cos, tan, log, square root and powers, and press equals to see the answer. Everything runs in your browser, so there is nothing to install.
content.tip: Trigonometry here uses degrees, so sin(30) is 0.5, the same as a school calculator in degree mode. Use brackets to control the order, such as (2+3) x 4, instead of relying on memory. Tap Back to remove one character instead of clearing the whole sum.
content.limit: Trigonometry uses degrees, not radians. Factorial only works for whole numbers from 0 to 170. Very long sums may be hard to read on a small screen, and the tool does not save your history.
content.example: Typing sin(30) and pressing = gives 0.5.
faq: Does sin use degrees or radians?
Degrees. Sin(30) gives 0.5, the same as a school calculator set to degrees. There is no radian mode on this page.
How do I work out a square root?
Tap sqrt, type the number, close the bracket if one opened, then press =. For example, sqrt(16) gives 4, and sqrt(2) gives about 1.4142.
What does the x squared key do?
It raises the number before it to the power of 2. Typing 5 then the squared key gives 25, and typing 10 then the squared key gives 100.
Can I use brackets in a sum?
Yes. Tap the bracket keys to group parts of the sum. For example, (2+3) x 4 gives 20, while 2+3 x 4 gives 14.

short.en: Add, subtract, multiply and divide fractions.

tools.meta_description: Add, subtract, multiply and divide fractions, simplified, with the decimal value.
steps: Type the first fraction as a top number and a bottom number.
Choose add, subtract, multiply or divide in the 'Operation' list.
Type the second fraction the same way.
Press Calculate Fraction, or just wait, because the result updates as you type.
Read the simplified fraction and its decimal value under the button.

content.use: Fraction Calculator adds, subtracts, multiplies and divides fractions and simplifies the answer. A student checks homework on adding halves and thirds. A cook halves a recipe that uses fractions of a cup. A worker splits a length into equal parts for a job. A teacher makes quick fraction questions for a class test without working them out by hand. You type the two fractions, choose the operation, and the tool shows the simplified fraction and its decimal value, so you can check your own working in seconds.
content.tip: The answer is always simplified, so 2/4 shows as 1/2. A whole number answer shows as a whole number, such as 2, not 2/1. For a mixed number, divide the top by the bottom yourself; for example 5/2 is 2 and 1/2.
content.limit: Only whole numbers are accepted in the top and bottom boxes. The bottom number cannot be zero, and dividing by a fraction of zero is not allowed. The decimal is rounded to 4 places.
content.example: 1/2 plus 1/3 equals 5/6, which is about 0.8333.
faq: How do I add 1/2 and 1/3?
Type 1 over 2, choose add, type 1 over 3, then press Calculate Fraction. The answer is 5/6, about 0.8333.
Why is the answer simplified?
The tool divides the top and bottom by their largest shared factor. That gives the simplest form, such as 1/2 instead of 2/4.
Can the bottom number be zero?
No. A fraction with zero on the bottom has no value, so the tool asks for a different number before it can work out the answer.
What does the decimal value mean?
It is the fraction as a decimal number. For 5/6 it is about 0.8333, rounded to 4 decimal places, which is easier to use on a calculator or a measuring tape.
